title: Tyvok Spider and Large-Format Lasers: When Diode Is Not Enough
metaDescription: Tyvok's Spider A1 (800x400 mm) and Spider X1S (800x2000 mm) for large work, and the Gweike Cloud G2 Pro fiber marker for metal, with prices from $349 to $1,543.98.
author: ByteBuy Team

sections.content: Most hobby laser engravers cover an area of about 400x400 mm and work on wood, leather and coated surfaces. This guide looks at two ways to go beyond that. The first is size: the Tyvok Spider A1 and X1S cover 800x400 mm and 800x2000 mm, big enough for signs, panels and long boards. The second is material: the Gweike Cloud G2 Pro is a fiber laser marker built for metal, which diode lasers handle poorly. The two solve different problems, and neither suits small hobby work.

pros: The Spider A1 offers an 800x400 mm area, twice the width of a typical 400 mm machine, for $349
The Spider X1S has an 800x2000 mm area and 20W for $799.99, a very large work surface for the price
The Gweike G2 Pro lists a stated 1.5 mm maximum depth on metal and 30+ colors, which diode lasers do not provide
The Gweike lists support for LightBurn and a rotary roller, so it fits common workflows
cons: The Spiders need a lot of space: an 800x2000 mm machine takes up a large part of a room, so measure before you buy
The Spider listings give only power and area, and say nothing about air assist, speed or safety features, so confirm them on the product page
The Gweike's 110x110 mm area is small, and at $1,543.98 it costs far more than any diode machine here
The Tyvok bed is 400x400 mm and is not described as fitting the Spider models, so do not assume compatibility
Large machines cut fast, which raises the fire risk, so supervision and ventilation matter even more

items.question: Who needs an 800x2000 mm laser?
items.answer: People who cut or engrave large pieces: signs, furniture panels, long boards or batches. If your projects fit on a 400 mm bed, a smaller machine is cheaper and easier to place.

items.question: What can a fiber laser do that a diode cannot?
items.answer: Fiber lasers are generally used to mark metals, and the Gweike lists a stated 1.5 mm maximum depth on metal. Diode lasers are better suited to wood, leather and coated materials. Choose the type by the material you work with.

items.question: Is the Gweike G2 Pro good for beginners?
items.answer: It is a specialized machine. It makes sense if you need to mark metal parts, tools or jewelry. For general crafts, a diode laser is simpler and far cheaper.

items.question: Spider A1 or X1S?
items.answer: The A1 is the lower-cost step into large format, at 10W and 800x400 mm. The X1S is for long pieces, with 20W and a 2000 mm length. Check the product pages for the rest of the specifications, because the listings are brief.

items.question: Do large lasers need extra safety?
items.answer: Yes. Use laser-rated eye protection, ventilation or an extractor, and never leave a running machine unattended. Our laser safety guide covers fire, fumes and eyes.

sections.content: Go large for size, go fiber for metal, and stay with a diode laser if neither applies. The Spider A1 and X1S make sense for big projects if you have the space, and the Gweike G2 Pro for marking metal. Read the product pages for details the listings leave out.
